_comment: D-CORE-11: protected system-seed mnemonics planted into every new tenant's global scope by the provisioning seeder. Canonical content pulled verbatim from the live johannesbayer.kumbuka.ai global scope (the dogfooding tenant). Update via a seed-content release; in-place edits to this file ship as the next kumbuka-server release and re-seed on next tenant provisioning + existing-tenant top-up via the manual seed call.

seeds.content: Kumbuka mnemonics are typed. Choose the type by intent. decision = a ratified choice; carries a stable ID (D-…, ADR-…) in key and content. constraint = a durable, binding rule every apparatus must obey; cross-cutting, not reversible by working preference. convention = a reversible working norm or style (this entry is one). status = the current steering state (sprint/gate/phase); keep it coarse — a small set of upsert-keyed entries rotated at phase changes, never fine-grained progress (that belongs in version control). glossary = a term definition. open_question = an unratified question awaiting a decision. Boundary: a durable, binding, cross-apparatus rule belongs in memory as type=constraint; boot mechanics and per-session instructions stay in the project's STARTER/context, not in memory. Never store speculation as decision or constraint — use open_question.

Writing mnemonics. Each is ONE self-contained fact, plaintext, ≤1500 chars — resist bloating the primitive (no embedded relations, scores, or rich metadata; heavyweight knowledge belongs in documents, not the atomic entry). Keys: lowercase, dot/kebab-namespaced (e.g. decision.d-ops-26, status.beta-gate); no underscores. Entries are insert-only (pre-V5): to revise, forget the old entry and remember a fresh one, and say so. Never store secrets, tokens, credentials, or third-party personal data.

Reading & scope. At the start of work, load_context once for the typed digest; use recall for topic lookups instead of guessing. Scope: unscoped reads return private + global only — project scopes require an explicit scope parameter (they are not leaked into unscoped reads). Write team-relevant facts to the project scope; private only on explicit request. Source-of-truth order when sources conflict: (1) the project's canonical spec/repo wins; (2) Kumbuka mnemonics are distilled, work-steering pointers; (3) chat context. If a mnemonic contradicts the spec, flag it as stale and propose a correction — do not follow it blindly.
